brief.title: Election update: Thursday, November 12 (morning)
brief.markdown:
# Election update: Thursday, November 12 (morning)

## Bottom line
The House results table marks 426 races called: D 257, R 169, with 218 needed for a majority ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). This morning's parse missed Delaware's at-large row, which the table marked called for Rep. Sarah McBride (D) on Wednesday, so the Democratic count is one seat low. In the Senate, Scott Colom (D) won Mississippi, the New York Times reports ([NYT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxPRTNHZFFRdHFUWjJ5Yk4xZGNtemYyR3B3UENkcHE3NG5TOUo3ai0ydnFGQ2k5YU1IbkNLdG4tNHR4dTZES01xQVlrMHN2YUdVUVJoQzNEcFdzN3N2Q1d0Z0lwZE1sM2I0dGFZY250Zk91QUtjczEtS1dsQTh0YjJ5MmpxZkltaGU0R2J3MXpqSzMxdw?oc=5)). That brings Democrats to 55 seats and Republicans to 44, counting seats not up, with Alaska the last uncalled race ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Governors: D 28, R 20 of 50, counting the 14 states with no race this year; Alaska and Kansas are not called, and five seats flipped, all to Democrats ([governor table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections)). Three seats rated Solid R came in within 5 points; Republicans held all three.

## Called since the last update
- **Flips (2, both D):** SEN-MS, where Colom unseated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) and became Mississippi's first Black senator in about 150 years, the BBC reports ([BBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE9GTWpzUWs1VjNiQ09nTDg5VjZ2eFh4aGxITHRBWmtybXRCekpoRHNkbkpuNGhoTng1NG1LV0U3Sm1sb0xBY0J3WjQzVVJweTd0UVB6VWxkX0pZMW8?oc=5)); HOU-NC-03, where Rep. Greg Murphy (R) conceded to Democrat Raymond Smith Jr. ([The Hill](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Hold (1, R):** HOU-SC-02 **(rated safe)**: Rep. Joe Wilson (R) won reelection after a recount confirmed a narrow victory, about 1 point in the table ([WLTX](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Rated safe, came in close:** OK-05 (Rep. Stephanie Bice, R, by 1.3 points) and OK-01 (Rep. Mark Tedford, R, by 4.6 points), both called for the Republicans in the table ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- No governor race was called.

## Still uncalled
One line for every competitive race the table hasn't marked called: Senate, then governors, then House.
- **SEN-AK** (Tossup): Mary Peltola (D) now has more votes than Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) and the other Republican combined, The Hill reports ([The Hill](https://news.google.?oc=5)); Alaska Public Media says the newest count tightened the Senate and governor races ([Alaska Public Media](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxNbXpyblpyZ0ZPendfLWRVTjlGMmNDeVpOcWZBT29aQUU2RWV3TVZtRzAxbzFtUGEtTEs4ZUNTaEtOUDNjYk5XWkZJd1RaYTZYQThhdFpYcUIxT0dTN0VrbFNSNExpUWZCdl9mNGhWMFpfMFJIR016bVBTdGZZVTQ2WXYxWk5lZFpLMWtNdi1VY29yeTRfR2tDX2hiNUdfRDg4RHJBLTZnTktodnNRS3RFWDRhMXlWTUNOVUhELXRleFg2dw?oc=5)).
- **GOV-KS** (Tilt R): Cindy Holscher (D) leads Ty Masterson (R) by 0.6 points in the table; KSN explains why the race is still too close to call ([KSN](https://news.google.?oc=5)). The state certifies Nov. 16 ([KWCH](https://www.kwch.com/2026/11/10/nearly-week-after-midterm-election-governors-race-is-still-too-close-call/)).
- **GOV-AK** (Lean D): Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D) leads the first round with 49.1% in the table, short of 50%, so ranked-choice tabulation is still pending ([governor table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections)); the Alaska Beacon says he is near victory after 25,000 more votes were counted ([Alaska Beacon](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxPaDRheGpFczN3anVBdVFMSHZPMTNMdm1Gd05aNGZGVmpJWG53RTY4RWVWQ3FWSkpUaFAzWXFLd2l4VmEtMGQ3YXRhdGhpSWhiemtfT1dmcFRTa3ItQ1JxWnFIa1dfZEVCcGFjTklycDBOZkVZTjBSNEg1WGgyZFpramNnLVdIeTlOOUJXbHZ4aGo5eEhRQXpzaUFaOTR4c1dOcVotRVlBTlc0UkM3TWEzWmpMN1JVbjdWZndNRFJR?oc=5)).
- **HOU-AK-AL** (Lean R): Rep. Nick Begich III (R) is also near victory, the Alaska Beacon reports ([Alaska Beacon](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxPaDRheGpFczN3anVBdVFMSHZPMTNMdm1Gd05aNGZGVmpJWG53RTY4RWVWQ3FWSkpUaFAzWXFLd2l4VmEtMGQ3YXRhdGhpSWhiemtfT1dmcFRTa3ItQ1JxWnFIa1dfZEVCcGFjTklycDBOZkVZTjBSNEg1WGgyZFpramNnLVdIeTlOOUJXbHZ4aGo5eEhRQXpzaUFaOTR4c1dOcVotRVlBTlc0UkM3TWEzWmpMN1JVbjdWZndNRFJR?oc=5)).
- **HOU-NC-05** (Likely R): Chuck Hubbard (D) appears to have ousted Rep. Virginia Foxx (R) as provisional and cured ballots were counted, NC Newsline reports; AP has not called it ([NC Newsline](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxNQVRxOUVETkstUElYQlJMUWdsRFlXX0JOdXF1U1Zua1FqdzdmNW56UU5RR2o3QWJuekVUVllfZEVQeHctOVAwVlZUekF6T09oU0gxTU1ZLWZKSmZ1ZThOQUthaFcwVHpqaFpuQmdNUHJESGtDWURzZDdhMFlYWUN4ZnFlbGp6NGpvaEczVGl1UmJfM2h4ZHBwdVpyNi15T2Mwb2lSSlhGWTRQeUV4ekZDcEpR?oc=5)).
- **HOU-NC-07** (Likely R): the race north of Charlotte has dipped into recount territory, the Charlotte Observer reports ([Charlotte Observer](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **HOU-MN-01** (Lean R): still uncalled; Minnesota is headed for a jump in recounts ([KSTP](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxNSDRZYzJvQ19XMnNDWWRISlVJSkdKbk9CRVd1czFhQUlmUHVoZXp4Y3oxVnREQ0I5QUYtWExmLUVBVFpyMkJTeHFDd3h3czZBVzNJVXJCZElLbjhQNGx6OWkzYXhHdF9xYWFDNXNZRkt5NmZQNHI1QXEzZTY0M2FZbU9Rd21hYndCMnI2MGt6SEt2MER2dU1xRjBKX3lhWUVQRFNvU3FTTQ?oc=5)).
- **Safe seats:** 4 seats rated safe are not yet marked in the table. That is table lag, not close races ([full list](https://jakeworcester-byte.github.io/political-tracker/#results)).

## Recounts and certification
- **South Carolina:** recounts confirmed the ouster of a legislative majority leader and a narrow Greenville County Republican win, the South Carolina Daily Gazette reports ([SC Daily Gazette](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **North Carolina:** NC-07 is within recount range, per the Charlotte Observer ([Charlotte Observer](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Kansas:** the state certifies Nov. 16; recount requests are due by 5 p.m. Nov. 17 ([KWCH](https://www.kwch.com/2026/11/10/nearly-week-after-midterm-election-governors-race-is-still-too-close-call/)).

## Legal and federal action
- **Alaska:** a judge dismissed the Peltola campaign's petition for the names of voters whose absentee ballots were rejected, the Alaska Beacon reports ([Alaska Beacon](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxQMTBfNzhKWm8xUDR4aW5UNGVURE5fOHhPZlN1QVlHcXAzMXV3dmg0LWNhdHNqWmlMQkZYM2J0SHlYLWdwakFtcVhpR3lfQW5qdFB4NDlpTjAxQ1FmMkVRRTNVdl9YUXdpc0EtNDRwS3hNMkc3ZEJaekUxRlh6YW0zV0o4MkJ2NGgxNU1IcTl4X2hjdE1kRGhNSWp4OHVkOWhQNnVtZjNta0NRbVp6bjE5elFxVVh3bzZRYXZhSUFWLVA?oc=5)); Reuters also reports the ruling ([Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixwFBVV95cUxOQWN5S25TbURDMXBFUXJPdmpKODcxdnRfM1dXOHQ5M1VHSlJtTzROQ3RpaVV6elVteUxOZ0Z3NVBZazNSQXM1bnZvLTE2dEprVjBFZTN0eTI2alZha2RLOTdfLTBwNGE4V05OQUlMQlMyZEVKcF9rMGZaTlZNMEF4YS1MSFJqUlFYNkNqbVU5X2xzMW1DNkRmbUxjSUNVU1BzTkRiOXo2NnA5N3Z1Rjc0TU1uaGtlak1lMUpQYXkyakJDOU5IUlVJ?oc=5)).
- **Federal dockets:** CourtListener shows activity in 36 election-related federal dockets since Nov. 9, including the FL-27 recount suit, Rodriguez v. Garcia ([CourtListener](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/75084109/rodriguez-v-garcia-et-al/)).

## What voters said
- **Turnout:** a surge in Michigan's college towns helped drive Democratic wins, the Detroit News reports ([Detroit News](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Voter surveys:** the New York Times breaks down how voters split by race, gender, age, and education ([NYT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigwFBVV95cUxPM1Jxc0lSUzI0NVB6SGd3d0tlX2R1akVfdmR6ejBVcndPNTFkNS1EQ1ZkNmJsRGh1bHZjZmlzeW0ySjRxcnpuY1FNY0RncVBwX2J3SmRzaGZGUFRUaG5ndEdhLWo0VVdTQmI1SHFqLTJxUkhSZUhIekNpN3FqOHhYV09fRQ?oc=5)). No new voter-file read from Ralston or Bitzer is in today's leads.

## Coverage note
- **Parser:** the Senate (35) and governor (36) tables parsed fully and the parser check is healthy. The House table parsed 434 of 435 rows; Delaware's at-large row was missed, so the House Democratic count is one low. The parser fix is left for an attended session.
- **Court records:** CourtListener used (4 requests; 36 election dockets and 2 opinions).
- **Scorecard:** 95.2% of competitive races called; Lessons learned returns weekly (next around Nov. 16).
